exercises.title: Vector operations
exercises.description: Given $a = (2, -1, 3)$ and $b = (1, 4, -2)$. Compute $a + b$ and $3a - 2b$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Vectors are added component by component and multiplied by numbers.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
When subtracting, mind the sign of each component individually: $9 - (-4) = 13$.

exercises.title: Length and unit vector
exercises.description: Compute the length: a) $(3, 4)$, b) $(1, 2, 2)$, c) $(-2, -2, 1)$. Determine the unit vector for a).
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$|v| = \sqrt{v_1^2 + v_2^2 + v_3^2}$. The unit vector is $\frac{v}{|v|}$.

Step 3: b) and c)
$\sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = 3$ and $\sqrt{4 + 4 + 1} = 3$.

Step 4: Unit vector for a)
$\frac{1}{5}(3, 4) = \left(\frac{3}{5}, \frac{4}{5}\right)$. Check: $\frac{9}{25} + \frac{16}{25} = 1$ ✓.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
Squares are always positive: for $(-2, -2, 1)$ the minus doesn't change the length.

exercises.title: Connecting vector and distance
exercises.description: Given $A(1, 2, 3)$ and $B(4, 6, 3)$. Determine $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and the distance between the points.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$\overrightarrow{AB} = B - A$ (“tip minus tail”). The distance is the length of this vector.

Step 2: Connecting vector
$\overrightarrow{AB} = (4 - 1,\ 6 - 2,\ 3 - 3) = (3, 4, 0)$.

Step 3: Distance
$|\overrightarrow{AB}| = \sqrt{9 + 16 + 0} = 5$.

Step 4: Check
$\overrightarrow{BA} = (-3, -4, 0)$ has the same length ✓.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
The order decides the direction, not the length.

exercises.title: Computing the dot product
exercises.description: Compute a) $(1, 2, 3) \cdot (4, -5, 6)$ and b) $(2, -1) \cdot (1, 2)$. What does the result in b) mean?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Dot product: add up the products of the components.

Step 3: b)
$2 \cdot 1 + (-1) \cdot 2 = 0$.

Step 4: Interpretation
Dot product $0$ means: the vectors are perpendicular to each other.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
The result is a number, not a vector.

exercises.title: Angle between vectors
exercises.description: Determine the angle between $a = (1, 0)$ and $b = (1, 1)$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$\cos\varphi = \frac{a \cdot b}{|a||b|}$.

Step 2: Dot product and lengths
$a \cdot b = 1$, $|a| = 1$, $|b| = \sqrt{2}$.

Step 3: Cosine
$\cos\varphi = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.

Step 4: Angle
$\varphi = 45°$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
Check with a sketch: $b$ is the diagonal of the unit square, i.e. at $45°$ to the $x$-axis ✓.

exercises.title: Orthogonality
exercises.description: Determine $t$ such that $(t, 2, 1)$ is perpendicular to $(1, -1, 4)$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Orthogonal means dot product $0$.

Step 2: Equation
$t \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot (-1) + 1 \cdot 4 = 0 \Rightarrow t + 2 = 0$.

Step 3: Solution
$t = -2$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
Orthogonality conditions are linear equations in the unknowns.

exercises.title: Simple cross products
exercises.description: Compute $(1, 0, 0) \times (0, 1, 0)$, $(2, 0, 0) \times (0, 3, 0)$ and $a \times a$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Formula: $(a_2 b_3 - a_3 b_2,\ a_3 b_1 - a_1 b_3,\ a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1)$.

Step 2: First product
$(0 - 0,\ 0 - 0,\ 1 \cdot 1 - 0) = (0, 0, 1)$.

Step 3: Second product
$(0, 0,\ 2 \cdot 3 - 0) = (0, 0, 6)$ – the length $6$ is the area of the $2 \times 3$ rectangle.

Step 4: $a \times a$
All components cancel: $a \times a = 0$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
The cross product of parallel vectors is the zero vector – a test for parallelism.

exercises.title: Line in the plane
exercises.description: Determine the line through $(1, 2)$ and $(3, 6)$ in parametric form and check whether $(5, 10)$ lies on it.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
The position vector is a point, the direction vector the difference of the points.

Step 3: Parametric form
$g: \ x = (1, 2) + t\,(2, 4)$.

Step 4: Point check
$1 + 2t = 5 \Rightarrow t = 2$. Second coordinate: $2 + 8 = 10$ ✓. The point lies on $g$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
The line is $y = 2x$: all its points satisfy $y = 2x$, including $(5, 10)$.

exercises.title: Angle in space
exercises.description: Determine the angle between $a = (1, 2, 2)$ and $b = (2, -1, 2)$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Compute the dot product and lengths, then form $\cos\varphi$.

Step 2: Dot product
$a \cdot b = 2 - 2 + 4 = 4$.

Step 3: Lengths
$|a| = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = 3$ and $|b| = \sqrt{4 + 1 + 4} = 3$.

Step 4: Cosine
$\cos\varphi = \frac{4}{9} \approx 0.444$.

Step 5: Angle
$\varphi = \arccos\frac{4}{9} \approx 63.6°$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
Positive dot product ⇒ acute angle. The angle always lies in $[0°, 180°]$.

exercises.title: Orthogonal projection
exercises.description: a) Project $b = (3, 2)$ onto $a = (4, 0)$. b) Project $b = (1, 2, 3)$ onto $a = (1, 1, 1)$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$\text{proj}_a(b) = \frac{a \cdot b}{|a|^2}\,a$.

Step 3: a) Check
The remainder $b - (3, 0) = (0, 2)$ is perpendicular to $a$: $(0, 2) \cdot (4, 0) = 0$ ✓.

Step 5: b) Check
The remainder $(1, 2, 3) - (2, 2, 2) = (-1, 0, 1)$ is perpendicular to $(1, 1, 1)$: $-1 + 0 + 1 = 0$ ✓.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
Projection plus remainder decompose $b$ into a parallel and a perpendicular part.

exercises.title: Area with the cross product
exercises.description: Compute the area of the parallelogram and of the triangle spanned by $a = (1, 2, 3)$ and $b = (4, 5, 6)$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
The length of the cross product is the parallelogram area, the triangle has half of it.

Step 2: Cross product
$a \times b = (2 \cdot 6 - 3 \cdot 5,\ 3 \cdot 4 - 1 \cdot 6,\ 1 \cdot 5 - 2 \cdot 4) = (-3, 6, -3)$.

Step 3: Length
$|a \times b| = \sqrt{9 + 36 + 9} = \sqrt{54} = 3\sqrt{6} \approx 7.35$.

Step 4: Areas
Parallelogram $\approx 7.35$, triangle $\frac{\sqrt{54}}{2} \approx 3.67$.

Step 5: Check of the perpendicularity
$a \cdot (a \times b) = -3 + 12 - 9 = 0$ ✓.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
The cross product is defined only in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

exercises.title: Line through two points in space
exercises.description: Determine the line through $A(1, 2, 3)$ and $B(3, 2, 5)$. Check whether $P(5, 2, 7)$ and $Q(2, 2, 3)$ lie on it.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Position vector $A$, direction $\overrightarrow{AB}$. Point check via the parameter.

Step 2: Line equation
$\overrightarrow{AB} = (2, 0, 2)$, so $g: \ x = (1, 2, 3) + t\,(2, 0, 2)$.

Step 3: $P$
$1 + 2t = 5 \Rightarrow t = 2$. Second coordinate $2$ ✓, third $3 + 4 = 7$ ✓. $P$ lies on $g$.

Step 4: $Q$
$1 + 2t = 2 \Rightarrow t = 0.5$. Third coordinate $3 + 1 = 4 \neq 3$. $Q$ does not lie on $g$.

Step 5: Note
It suffices to solve ONE coordinate for $t$ and check the others.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
All three coordinate equations must hold with the same $t$.

exercises.title: Intersecting lines
exercises.description: Examine the relative position of $g: (1, 2, 0) + t(1, 1, 1)$ and $h: (2, 3, 1) + s(0, 1, 2)$. Determine the intersection point if it exists.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
The direction vectors are not multiples. So equate: three equations for $t, s$.

Step 3: Solve
From the first $t = 1$. Second: $3 = 3 + s \Rightarrow s = 0$. Third: $1 = 1 + 0$ ✓.

Step 4: Intersection point
$t = 1$ in $g$: $(2, 3, 1)$. With $s = 0$ in $h$: $(2, 3, 1)$ ✓.

Step 5: Result
The lines intersect at $S = (2, 3, 1)$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
The third equation serves as a check: if it fails, the lines are skew.

exercises.title: Skew lines
exercises.description: Show that $g: t(1, 0, 0)$ and $h: (0, 1, 0) + s(0, 0, 1)$ are skew and determine their distance.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Directions not parallel, no common point. Distance via the common normal vector.

Step 2: Not parallel
$(1, 0, 0)$ and $(0, 0, 1)$ are not multiples.

Step 3: No intersection
$g$ always has $y = 0$, $h$ always $y = 1$. Equating leads to $0 = 1$ – skew.

Step 4: Normal vector
$n = (1, 0, 0) \times (0, 0, 1) = (0 \cdot 1 - 0 \cdot 0,\ 0 \cdot 0 - 1 \cdot 1,\ 0) = (0, -1, 0)$.

Step 5: Distance
Connection of the anchor points $(0, 1, 0)$; projection onto $n$: $\frac{|(0, 1, 0) \cdot (0, -1, 0)|}{1} = 1$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
The distance of skew lines is the length of the shortest connection – it is perpendicular to both directions.

exercises.title: Plane from three points
exercises.description: Determine the coordinate equation of the plane through $A(1, 0, 0)$, $B(0, 1, 0)$, $C(0, 0, 1)$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Two direction vectors, their cross product as the normal vector, then $d$ by substituting a point.

Step 2: Directions
$\overrightarrow{AB} = (-1, 1, 0)$, $\overrightarrow{AC} = (-1, 0, 1)$.

Step 3: Normal vector
$n = (1 \cdot 1 - 0 \cdot 0,\ 0 \cdot (-1) - (-1) \cdot 1,\ (-1) \cdot 0 - 1 \cdot (-1)) = (1, 1, 1)$.

Step 4: Equation
$x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = d$, with $A$: $d = 1$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
The plane $x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = 1$ meets every axis at $1$ – visible from the equation too.

exercises.title: Distance point–plane
exercises.description: Determine the distance of $P(2, 2, 2)$ from the plane $E: x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = 1$. Does $(1, 0, 0)$ lie in $E$?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$d(P, E) = \frac{|n \cdot P - d|}{|n|}$ with $n = (1, 1, 1)$, $d = 1$.

Step 2: Numerator
$n \cdot P - d = 6 - 1 = 5$.

Step 3: Denominator
$|n| = \sqrt{3}$.

Step 4: Distance
$d = \frac{5}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 2.89$.

Step 5: Point check
$(1, 0, 0)$: $1 + 0 + 0 = 1$ ✓, the point lies in $E$ (distance $0$).

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
The absolute value in the numerator makes sure the distance is never negative.

exercises.title: Intersection of a line and a plane
exercises.description: Determine the intersection point of the line $g: (1, 0, -1) + t(1, 2, 1)$ with the plane $E: 2x_1 + x_2 - x_3 = 4$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Substitute the coordinates of the line into the plane equation and solve for $t$.

Step 3: Solve
$2 + 2t + 2t + 1 - t = 3 + 3t = 4 \Rightarrow t = \frac{1}{3}$.

Step 4: Intersection point
$\left(\frac{4}{3}, \frac{2}{3}, -\frac{2}{3}\right)$.

Step 5: Check
$2 \cdot \frac{4}{3} + \frac{2}{3} + \frac{2}{3} = \frac{12}{3} = 4$ ✓.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
Exactly one $t$: intersection point. $0 = 0$: line lies in the plane. $0 = c \neq 0$: line parallel to the plane.

exercises.title: Distance point–line in space
exercises.description: Determine the distance of $P(3, 0, 0)$ from the line $g: t\,(1, 2, 2)$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Formula: $d = \frac{|u \times w|}{|u|}$ with direction vector $u$ and connecting vector $w$ from the anchor point to $P$.

Step 3: Cross product
$u \times w = (2 \cdot 0 - 2 \cdot 0,\ 2 \cdot 3 - 1 \cdot 0,\ 1 \cdot 0 - 2 \cdot 3) = (0, 6, -6)$.

Step 4: Lengths
$|u \times w| = \sqrt{72} = 6\sqrt{2}$ and $|u| = 3$.

Step 5: Distance
$d = \frac{6\sqrt{2}}{3} = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.83$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
Geometrically: $|u \times w|$ is the parallelogram area from $u$ and $w$; divided by the base $|u|$ it gives the height – the distance.

exercises.title: Perpendicular onto a line
exercises.description: Determine the foot of the perpendicular from $P(1, 1)$ onto the line $x + y = 4$ and the distance.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
The perpendicular has the direction of the normal vector $n = (1, 1)$ of the line.

Step 2: Perpendicular line
$l: \ (1, 1) + t\,(1, 1) = (1 + t, 1 + t)$.

Step 3: Intersection
Substitute into $x + y = 4$: $2 + 2t = 4 \Rightarrow t = 1$.

Step 4: Foot point
$F = (2, 2)$.

Step 5: Distance
$|\overrightarrow{PF}| = |(1, 1)| = \sqrt{2}$. With the formula: $\frac{|1 + 1 - 4|}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}$ ✓.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
The foot point is the point of the line closest to $P$.

exercises.title: Schwarz and triangle inequality
exercises.description: Check for $a = (1, 2)$ and $b = (3, -1)$ the inequalities $|a \cdot b| \le |a||b|$ and $|a + b| \le |a| + |b|$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
We compute both sides. The Schwarz inequality follows from $|\cos\varphi| \le 1$.

Step 2: Dot product and lengths
$a \cdot b = 3 - 2 = 1$, $|a| = \sqrt{5}$, $|b| = \sqrt{10}$.

Step 3: Schwarz
$|a \cdot b| = 1 \le \sqrt{5}\sqrt{10} = \sqrt{50} \approx 7.07$ ✓.

Step 4: Triangle inequality
$a + b = (4, 1)$, $|a + b| = \sqrt{17} \approx 4.12$. Right: $\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{10} \approx 2.24 + 3.16 = 5.40$. $4.12 \le 5.40$ ✓.

Step 5: Equality
For parallel, same-direction vectors equality holds, e.g. $b = 2a$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
Both inequalities are the basis for norms and distances in general vector spaces.

exercises.title: Rhombus and diagonals
exercises.description: Show: in a rhombus the diagonals are perpendicular. Check it for $a = (3, 4)$, $b = (4, 3)$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
A rhombus has equal sides $|a| = |b|$. The diagonals are $a + b$ and $a - b$.

Step 2: Dot product
$(a + b) \cdot (a - b) = a \cdot a - a \cdot b + b \cdot a - b \cdot b = |a|^2 - |b|^2$.

Step 3: Consequence
Since $|a| = |b|$, the dot product is $0$: the diagonals are orthogonal. $\square$

Step 5: Converse
If $(a + b) \cdot (a - b) = 0$, then $|a| = |b|$ – the parallelogram is a rhombus.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
Proofs with vectors are often short computations with the dot product – without any sketch.

exercises.title: Volume of a parallelepiped
exercises.description: Compute the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $a = (1, 0, 0)$, $b = (1, 2, 0)$ and $c = (1, 1, 3)$ using the scalar triple product $V = |a \cdot (b \times c)|$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
The cross product $b \times c$ gives the base area (magnitude) and the direction of the height; the dot product with $a$ gives the height component.

Step 2: Cross product
$b \times c = (2 \cdot 3 - 0 \cdot 1,\ 0 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 3,\ 1 \cdot 1 - 2 \cdot 1) = (6, -3, -1)$.

Step 3: Dot product
$a \cdot (b \times c) = 1 \cdot 6 + 0 + 0 = 6$.

Step 4: Volume
$V = |6| = 6$.

Step 5: Plausibility
The matrix of $a, b, c$ is triangular with diagonal $1, 2, 3$: product $6$ ✓ (determinant).

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
The scalar triple product is the determinant of the three vectors. If it is $0$, the vectors lie in one plane.

exercises.title: Perpendicular planes
exercises.description: Show that the planes $E_1: x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = 1$ and $E_2: x_1 - x_2 = 0$ are perpendicular, and determine their line of intersection.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Two planes are perpendicular if their normal vectors are perpendicular. The line of intersection solves both equations.

Step 3: Intersection
From $E_2$: $x_1 = x_2$. Then $E_1$: $2x_1 + x_3 = 1$, so $x_3 = 1 - 2x_1$.

Step 5: Check
Direction $(1, 1, -2)$ is perpendicular to both normals: $1 + 1 - 2 = 0$ ✓ and $1 - 1 + 0 = 0$ ✓.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
The direction of the line of intersection is $n_1 \times n_2$ (parallel to both planes).

exercises.title: Work as a dot product
exercises.description: A force $F = (3, 4)$ N displaces a body by $s = (5, 0)$ m. a) Compute the work $W = F \cdot s$. b) A force of $10\,\text{N}$ acts at $30°$ to the direction of travel over $4\,\text{m}$. How much work is done?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Work is the dot product of force and displacement – only the force component along the path counts.

Step 2: a)
$W = 3 \cdot 5 + 4 \cdot 0 = 15\,\text{J}$.

Step 3: Interpretation a)
The force component in $x$-direction is $3\,\text{N}$, times $5\,\text{m}$ gives $15\,\text{J}$. The $y$-component does no work.

Step 4: b)
$W = |F||s|\cos 30° = 10 \cdot 4 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.64\,\text{J}$.

Step 5: Plausibility
Without the angle it would be $40\,\text{J}$. The angle reduces the work to $\cos 30° \approx 87\,\%$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
If the force is perpendicular to the path ($\cos 90° = 0$), no work is done – e.g. on a circular path.
